I am 54 years old and I have farmed here in Quzhou County all my life. I only went to primary school, but I know this land and this climate. I have 8 mu of irrigated land, and I do what has always worked here on the North China Plain: winter wheat followed by summer maize. Two crops a year, every year.

Last October I already sowed my wheat — I use Luyuan 502, an improved variety that yields steady and does not fail me. I rotary-tilled the soil before sowing and put down compound fertilizer as a basal dressing. Now that spring is starting, I will topdress with urea when the wheat greens up. I will irrigate three times — spring green-up, jointing, and flowering — and spray four times total for insects, weeds, and disease. I expect about 500 kg per mu.

Right after I harvest the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant Denghai 605 hybrid maize directly into the wheat stubble without tilling. No-tillage saves me time and diesel, and this hybrid seed gives good yield. I will apply compound fertilizer at sowing, irrigate twice over the summer, and spray three times for pests. I expect about 550 kg per mu.

I do not grow cotton — it is too much labor and the price jumps around too much. I also do not want to risk new crops I do not understand. Wheat and maize are certain. I know the inputs, I know the timing, and I know the buyers. At my age, with my schooling, I do not gamble with the land.
